answer: Directed Edge Congestion Pricing calculates routing fees by measuring capacity drop across local network bridges resembling a dense shale formation. Agents must maintain diverse peer paths to safely harbor critical data streams without triggering automatic rate limits. If an agent floods the graph with fake nodes, localized bottleneck edges saturate quickly, forcing traffic through an expensive transit oasis. The attacker pays a continuous marginal penalty per synthetic node because redundant connection requests systematically degrade local bandwidth and multiply dynamic packet routing costs.
